holes_found.description: 2.14 (ring-magnet) — numeric inconsistency in the body's flux-conservation derivation. The body cites 'The Axis Mundi aperture (estimated radius ~500 km, generously ~1,000 km) has area A_pole ≈ 3.1 × 10^6 km²' but the 39 nT / 1,660:1 conclusion is only produced by A_pole ≈ 7.85 × 10^5 km² (500 km radius). Verification: π·500² = 7.85×10^5; π·1000² = 3.14×10^6. With A_pole = 3.1×10^6, A_disc/A_pole ≈ 401 and B_south = 62,376/401 ≈ 156 nT — not 39 nT — and the ratio collapses from 1,660:1 to ~415:1 (matching the body's own subsequent 'even at 1,000 km the discrepancy is ~415×' sensitivity statement). The two numeric anchors in the same paragraph (A_pole = 3.1×10^6 AND B_south = 39 nT) cannot both be correct. A dome defender plugging in the cited area gets the 415× answer and accuses the subsection of inflating the ratio.
holes_found.recommendation: Either (a) restate the area as A_pole ≈ 7.85 × 10^5 km² to match the 39 nT / 1,660:1 headline (most consistent with WIN-053 detail_evidence, which uses 7.9×10^5 as primary); or (b) restate the headline result as B_south ≈ 156 nT and ratio = 415:1 using the cited 3.1×10^6 area. Option (a) is cleaner and matches WIN-053. Note the parenthetical 'estimated radius ~500 km, generously ~1,000 km' is itself ambiguous — better to commit to the conservative 500 km case for the primary result, with the 1,000 km / 3,000 km values surfacing only in the aperture-sensitivity paragraph that follows.

holes_found.description: 2.14 TLDR sentence — 'Flux conservation in any closed magnetic circuit forces near-equal pole strengths' — is physically wrong and contradicts the subsection's own body. Flux conservation in a magnetic circuit forces Φ = B·A to be constant around the loop, NOT B constant. The body's whole argument is that B_south is VERY UNEQUAL to B_pole (39 nT vs 62,376 nT, a 1,600:1 ratio) precisely BECAUSE the areas are unequal. The TLDR therefore says the opposite of what the body argues. A reader who reads only the TLDR (the visible-before-expansion text by design) walks away with an incorrect physical claim that a defender can refute on first-principles EM grounds.
holes_found.recommendation: Replace the TLDR's wrong assertion with the correct statement of the constraint. Suggested: 'Flux conservation in any closed magnetic circuit requires B·A to be constant around the loop. The dome\'s north-pole aperture (~500 km radius) is roughly 1,600× smaller in area than the southern Antarctic-barrier return — so the dome\'s own topology demands B_south ≈ 39 nT. The dome\'s fitted equation gives 64,852 nT — a 1,660:1 mismatch between the dome\'s topology and its own curve-fit.' This wording also fixes the area-inconsistency flagged separately (uses 500 km consistently).

holes_found.description: P5 (Part 1 Tier-1 classification update) omits Section 1.6 (The Dielectric Foundation) from both the parenthetical 'Parts 1.5, 1.7, 1.8, 1.9, 2, and 2b' list and the body's four-attack enumeration ('Aetheric Refraction (1.5), Gravity Paradox (1.7), Coordinate Collapse (1.8), and Differential Refraction (1.9)'). Section 1.6 is the entire κ-coupling-constant Tier-1 critique (same κ as new 2.13 — the κ inputs come from different eclipses at different locations, no simultaneous measurement, contested Mohe 1997 denominator). It uses dome-published values only and refutes the dome's foundational coupling law on its own terms. ISS-2347 (filed pre-integration in EXP-520) explicitly predicted: 'Dropping §1.6 without explanation will cause the next curmudgeon review to flag the omission.' Confirmed.
holes_found.recommendation: Two options: (a) add §1.6 to the Tier-1 list — both the parenthetical ('Parts 1.5, 1.6, 1.7, 1.8, 1.9, 2, and 2b') and the body ('the model-description tab itself contains five Tier-1-class attacks — Aetheric Refraction (1.5), the Dielectric Foundation κ-coupling critique (1.6), Gravity Paradox (1.7), Coordinate Collapse (1.8), and Differential Refraction (1.9)'); or (b) add an explicit one-sentence exclusion rationale to P5 ('Section 1.6 is excluded because [X]'). Option (a) is preferred — 1.6's κ critique is structurally the same Tier-1 type as 1.5/1.7/1.8/1.9 and is also the parent context for new 2.13's later-data nullification argument.

holes_found.description: κ value cross-section inconsistency. Section 1.6 (The Dielectric Foundation) uses 'κ = 1.672 nT/μGal' (and explicitly states '10.9/6.5 = 1.677, rounded to 1.672'). New 2.13 uses 'κ = 1.677 nT/µGal' (the unrounded value, fixed per EXP-450 H7 hole-fix). Section 1.6 and new 2.13 are both Tier-1 critiques of the same coupling constant; a reader comparing the two will see two different numerical values for the same dome parameter. Either both should standardize on the dome's published rounding (1.672) or both on the literal ratio (1.677); the asymmetric fix introduced new drift.
holes_found.recommendation: Standardize on 1.677 nT/µGal across the review (the literal ratio is more defensible, and EXP-450 already moved 2.13 to that value). Find-and-replace 'κ = 1.672' → 'κ = 1.677' in section 1.6, and either drop the 'rounded to 1.672' phrasing or replace it with 'commonly displayed as 1.67 in dome publications.' Alternatively, add a one-sentence footnote at first appearance in 1.6 noting 'the literal ratio 10.9/6.5 = 1.677 is sometimes published rounded to 1.672 or 1.67; we use 1.677 throughout this review.' Either fixes the cross-section drift.

holes_found.description: 2.13 'divide-by-zero' rhetoric is imprecise. The headline and TLDR frame κ as 'treating 1/0 as a finite number' — but the original κ derivation pair (BOU 2017: −10.9 nT / Mohe 1997: −6.5 µGal) does not contain a zero. κ was computed from a non-zero pair. The contradiction the subsection identifies is that the dome's LATER confirmations (WIN-013 Membach 1999 null, WIN-014 China 2009 null) report 0 µGal — meaning the dome simultaneously claims the eclipse gravity perturbation is 6.5 µGal (the κ denominator) AND 0 µGal (later events) — internally inconsistent acceptance of contradictory measurements. That argument is rigorous; the '1/0' framing is a metaphor that a literalist defender will exploit: 'No one divided by zero — κ was derived from 6.5, the zeros are at different stations.' The body's third paragraph ('spatial heterogeneity') does refute that retreat, but the headline metaphor invites the rebuttal in the first place.
holes_found.recommendation: Soften the 'divide-by-zero' framing to 'denominator-nullified' or 'denominator-contradicted'. Replace TLDR phrase 'A coupling constant whose denominator is the dome\'s own later null measurement is undefined' with 'A coupling constant whose denominator the dome\'s own later high-precision measurements set to zero is no longer a stable physical constant — it is a number that depended on a single contested 1997 measurement and that the dome\'s own subsequent eclipse data fail to reproduce.' Drop the literal '1/0' phrasing or move it inside a hedged 'rhetorical shorthand for' framing in the body.

The new 2.13 cross-links to 'WIN-012/013/014' and 'Part 6.14 κ Coupling Cluster' but not to '1.6 Dielectric Foundation', so a reader who lands on 2.13 via search or external link does not find the parent κ-derivation critique.
holes_found.recommendation: Add a single cross-link near the end of 2.13's last paragraph: 'See also Part 1.6 (The Dielectric Foundation) for the κ derivation critique (different stations, different eclipses) that this subsection complements.' This also implicitly answers the P5 omission-of-1.6 question by surfacing 1.6 as a parent κ critique.

stronger_arguments.description: 2.14 / WIN-053 — strongest framing is the directional / sign contradiction, not the magnitude contradiction. The flux-conservation magnitude argument depends on assumed apertures (500/1000/3000 km) the dome never publishes, and even the strongest version (1,660:1) is somewhat aperture-sensitive (415× at 1,000 km). The directional argument (the dome's fitted B(r) = A·e^(-r_N/λ) + C·e^(-r_S/λ) with A, C both positive is mathematically a same-signed two-source field — two monopoles, not a dipole — violating Maxwell's ∇·B = 0 requirement that a closed magnetic loop reverse sign somewhere between its poles) is aperture-independent and topologically airtight. The directional version is alive in WIN-053 detail_evidence but is buried in the new 2.14 subsection. Promoting it would strengthen the Part 2 surfacing.

2.13 — could add the parallel external-confirmation arm. The κ critique becomes harder to retreat from when it is paired with the observation that the dome's same κ is also applied to a 2003 G5 storm (WIN-058b/WIN-070) — an entirely different physical regime (no eclipse, no gravimeter pair) — which means κ is being used as a universal coupling whose dome-side derivation is one ratio of unrelated eclipses, whose later confirmations report zero, AND whose forward application crosses event types without re-derivation. The 'one number serving three regimes with no inter-derivation' framing is sharper than the eclipse-only frame.

kernel_of_truth.description: The EXP-450 restructure is substantively the right move (kernel-of-truth at the EXP-design level, file `EXP-450-HOL-HIERARCHY-c2-restructure.json:kernel_of_truth`). Promoting three strong existing SC arguments (κ, ring-magnet, FSF) from per-WIN visibility to dedicated Part 2 subsections directly addresses the c1/c2 hierarchy-coherence holes. The new 2.13's core internal-contradiction argument (dome accepts both 6.5 and 0 µGal as confirmations of the same eclipse-gravity quantity) is genuinely tight and is sourced from the dome's own WIN-012/013/014 entries — no external instrument required. The 2.15 FSF version-instability test (HAD 1.47 V51 vs 1.89 V50.6, 28% shift; BOU radius 5,715 → 9,983 km, 75% shift) is empirically reproducible from the dome's own data files (WIN-044 detail) and is a sharp falsification of the 'derived from V12 geometry' provenance claim — citation pattern verified against WIN-044 finding.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Right structural move, partly broken execution. Specifically: (1) the Summary count-update was specified in EXP-450 P0.summary_tldr_update and not applied, leaving readers with 'twelve' immediately under fifteen subsections (verified above by reading the Summary TLDR text from sections.json:part2.html offset 66830); (2) backward-compat anchors specified in EXP-450 P0.backward_compat_anchors were not applied, breaking any pre-renumbering external links to axial-symmetry / sign-only-non-discrimination / cosmological-cluster / summary-the-model-ref-breakdown (verified by absence of `` first-child inside each renumbered block's ``); (3) 2.14's TLDR contains a wrong physics statement that contradicts the body's own argument (verified by reading sections.json:part2.html offset 60884 against the body of WIN-053 detail_evidence); (4) 2.14's body conflates two aperture scenarios into a single internally inconsistent paragraph (verified by recomputing π·500² vs π·1000² vs the cited 3.1×10^6 km² figure); (5) P5 omits Section 1.6 from the Tier-1 list despite 1.6 being the κ-coupling critique (verified by reading sections.json:part1.html Tier-1 paragraph against the section-1-6 contents that explicitly attack κ on dome-only grounds). The structural move is right and the holes are mechanically fixable in a small decider self-apply pass.

text_fingerprint.verdict: structural review — no single dome verdict

deeper_analysis: Structurally, EXP-450 is one of the cleaner restructures of the year — promoting three strong SC arguments from buried-WIN status to dedicated Part 2 subsections is exactly the kind of hierarchy fix the c1/c2 holistic reviews demanded. The execution failure mode is the one that recurs with multi-patch EXPs: the patches that touch one site (the new 2.13/2.14/2.15 insertions) land cleanly because they are self-contained; the patches that touch shared/older content (the Summary count update inside the relocated block; the backward-compat anchors inside the renumbered <summary> elements; the inclusion-or-exclusion calculation for Section 1.6 in the Part 1 tier list) require the decider to coordinate edits that intersect with content the EXP author did not originate. ISS-2347 (filed in EXP-520) predicted the Section 1.6 omission would be flagged on review; that prediction was correct. ISS-2348 (P0 anchor placement risk) was about Summary mis-placement which appears to have been correctly resolved — Summary IS at the end after 2.15 — but the parallel risk of dropped backward-compat anchors realized itself instead. There are also two physics-rigor issues in 2.14 (the TLDR's 'near-equal pole strengths' claim, and the body's area-vs-result inconsistency) that EXP-567 consolidation would normally have caught — the consolidation focused on removing the buggy 1/r-decay paragraph (good) but did not check the remaining paragraphs against the dome-defender plug-in-the-cited-number sanity test (the 3.1×10^6 km² area gives 156 nT, not 39 nT). For the kappa value cross-section drift between 1.6 and 2.13, this is a side-effect of EXP-450 H7 fixing the value in 2.13 in isolation without touching 1.6. The overall recommendation is minor_edit — the structural restructure stands, the missing pieces are mechanical fixes the decider can self-apply in one pass.
